items.passage: Four hours a day, six days a week, no recordings: those were Ananya's conditions when she agreed to teach me. We met in the guesthouse of a small monastery on the edge of Mumbai, where the monks let her use a whitewashed room in exchange for playing at their evening prayers. She taught a way of tuning and bowing that her own teacher had learned in a village whose name I could not find on any map. Nobody else I knew played like that anymore. When I asked why she would not let me record her, she said a tape would teach my ears but not my hands. Vikram, she would say, again, and correct my wrist with a pencil tap until I hated the sound of it. Only much later did I see that the old style lived in her fingers like a language with one speaker left.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a language with one speaker left” most nearly suggests that the old style was
options: a technique so complex that it needed translation
a kind of music Ananya refused to share with others
a rare practice kept alive almost entirely by one person
a habit Ananya found difficult to explain in words
items.explanation: 지문은 그 연주법이 지도에도 없는 마을에서 전해졌고 이제 그렇게 연주하는 사람이 거의 없다고 말한다. 따라서 화자 한 명만 남은 언어라는 비유는 거의 한 사람에 의해서만 이어지는 사라져 가는 기술을 뜻하며 C가 정답이다. A는 '언어'를 번역과 연결한 오답이고, B는 녹음을 거부한 점만 보고 Ananya가 직접 가르친다는 사실을 놓친 것이다. D는 그녀가 말 대신 손으로 가르친 장면을 지나치게 해석한 것이다.

items.passage: So you let me win, Edith said, the moment Faisal stepped onto the old stone bridge. They had not spoken in nine years, not since the summer their grandmother set them to race across the Cornish headland for her silver whistle. Faisal had been faster; everyone knew it. Yet a stride from the bridge he had stumbled, and Edith had touched the parapet first. Now the grandmother lay in the churchyard behind them, and the whistle hung at Edith's neck. All these years, she said, the prize had felt like borrowed bread, filling her mouth but never her stomach. Faisal looked down at the river. He told her he had seen how badly she needed something of her own that year. Edith unhooked the whistle and pressed it into his palm, and for once he did not give it back.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “borrowed bread” most nearly suggests that Edith's victory was
options: a gift she had been eager to return to her grandmother long ago
a reward she had always been required to share with Faisal
a prize whose value faded slowly as she grew older
a win she could not fully enjoy because it was not earned
items.explanation: Edith는 더 빠른 Faisal이 결승 직전에 일부러 넘어져 이겼다는 사실을 알고 있었다. 빌린 빵이 입은 채워도 배는 채우지 못했다는 표현은 스스로 얻지 않은 승리라 진정한 만족을 주지 못했다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 할머니에게 돌려주려 했다는 근거가 없고, B는 '빌렸다'를 공유로 오해한 것이다. C는 시간이 흐르며 가치가 줄었다는 해석으로, 처음부터 공허했다는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Smell of wet soil and crushed shiso rose around them as Shigeru and Chiyo knelt in their plot of the community garden in Kyoto, pulling weeds between the rows of eggplant. For an hour they joked about their last concert, where the audience had numbered eleven, including a sleeping baby, and Chiyo imitated the hall manager's sigh until Shigeru dropped his trowel laughing. Then she mentioned the letter. A conservatory in Vienna had offered her a full scholarship beginning in January; it covered one student, not a duo. Shigeru went on weeding. He asked, evenly, when she would need to answer, and whether her cello would travel in the hold or on a seat. Each question was polite and practical, and each one seemed to set him a little further from her.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From bitter complaint about the concert to warm encouragement
From playful teasing to guarded restraint after Chiyo's news
From nervous tension to calm acceptance of a shared plan
From nostalgic reflection to open celebration of Chiyo's success
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 두 사람은 관객 열한 명이었던 공연을 두고 농담하며 웃는다. Chiyo가 혼자만 받을 수 있는 장학금 소식을 꺼내자 Shigeru는 담담하고 실무적인 질문만 하며 감정을 감춘다. 따라서 장난스러운 분위기에서 절제되고 경계하는 분위기로 바뀌는 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 격려나 축하를, C는 함께 세운 계획을 말하지만 지문의 거리감과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Once, I loved the library on Central Avenue
for its hush, its radiators ticking like patient clocks,
the way Elan would leave me in the stacks
and read the paper by the window, never hurrying.
We had a rhythm there: I chose, he signed.
Then on a Saturday in March he said,
between the atlases and the encyclopedias,
that he had sold the house, that we would move
to Denver in June, that it was settled.
Settled. As if I were a column he had added.
Now the radiators only hiss.
The books lean on each other like strangers in a line.
I, Nayeli, twelve, take down a map
and trace a road I did not choose.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the poem?
options: From restless boredom to eager curiosity about a new city
From quiet fear to comforting reassurance from Elan
From fond nostalgia to resentful bitterness after Elan's news
From playful humor to calm resignation about the move
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 도서관의 고요함과 Elan과의 리듬을 애정 어린 회상으로 그린다. Elan이 묻지도 않고 이사를 결정했다고 말한 뒤, 화자는 'Settled'를 되뇌며 자신을 더해진 숫자 한 줄에 비유하고, 라디에이터는 '쉭쉭거리기만' 한다. 따라서 애정 어린 그리움에서 원망 섞인 씁쓸함으로 바뀌는 C가 정답이다. D는 체념으로 보일 수 있지만 원망이 드러나는 표현을 놓쳤고, A와 B는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
BARTOLO: They printed your name alone, Judge, on the front page.
(Evening. The iron gate of a cemetery in Surabaya. LAN, a retired judge, leans on her cane. BARTOLO, her young clerk, holds a folded newspaper.)
LAN: (lightly) Newspapers like a single name. It fits the column better.
BARTOLO: I drafted three hundred pages of that opinion. You know I did.
LAN: (still amused) And I signed them. That is how it is done, my boy.
BARTOLO: My father is buried here. I promised him our family name would mean something one day. (He holds out the paper.) Read it to him.
(LAN stops smiling. A long pause. She takes the newspaper, studies it, then lowers it.)
LAN: (quietly) Give me your pen. Tomorrow I will write to the editor myself, and the correction will carry both our names.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From fierce anger to forced cheerfulness at the gate
From shared grief to hopeful celebration of the ruling
From formal respect to open hostility between the two
From dismissive amusement to sober acknowledgment of the clerk
items.explanation: 처음에 Lan은 '가볍게', '여전히 재미있다는 듯' 말하며 Bartolo의 기여를 관행이라고 넘긴다. Bartolo가 아버지의 무덤 앞에서 신문을 읽어 달라고 하자, 지문은 Lan이 웃음을 멈추고 오래 침묵한 뒤 '조용히' 말한다고 지시한다. 따라서 무시하는 듯한 여유에서 진지한 인정으로 바뀌는 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 분노, 축하, 적대감처럼 지문에 없는 감정을 내세운다.

items.passage: Three chairs, two mirrors, one radio tuned to the shipping forecast: that is the whole of Winston's barbershop on a narrow lane in Taipei, and for years I came less for the haircut than for his stories. He had been a sailor for thirty years, and he told those years like jokes: the typhoon off Okinawa, the cook who kept a parrot, the captain who could not swim. Last month, when I came in, Bokhee from the noodle stall next door was already in the chair, and Winston was laughing at something she had said. Then she asked about his nephew's boat, the one that had gone out in August and come back with half its crew. Winston set the scissors down. He finished her haircut without another word, and when I took her place, he cut my hair the way one folds a letter one does not want to reread.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From lively storytelling to heavy silence when a recent loss is raised
From bitter regret to amused acceptance of his years at sea
From casual friendliness to open anger at Bokhee's rudeness
From nervous chatter to calm confidence about his nephew's future
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Winston은 30년 항해를 농담처럼 들려주고 Bokhee의 말에 웃는다. Bokhee가 선원 절반을 잃고 돌아온 조카의 배를 묻자 그는 가위를 내려놓고 아무 말 없이 머리를 마저 자른다. 따라서 활기찬 이야기에서 무거운 침묵으로 바뀌는 A가 정답이다. B는 변화 방향이 반대이고, C의 분노와 D의 자신감은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage: Carmela was the name on my badge that winter, though the keepers at the lighthouse station outside Tbilisi mostly called me 'the voice.' I interpreted for Pavel, a Czech engineer hired to inspect the old signal lamp, which now guided nothing but the fishing boats that crossed the reservoir at night. On our first morning, the station chief explained the rule: visitors could not climb above the third landing without a keeper beside them, and the keepers never had time. I translated this briskly, as I had translated a hundred regulations, and Pavel nodded the way people nod at weather. By the fourth day, though, I had watched him wait on that landing for hours, his notebook open to blank pages, while the keepers drank tea below and shrugged. When the chief repeated the rule yet again, I heard my own voice go flat and careful, choosing each word as if it might break. I did not soften it this time. I let him hear exactly how little sense it made.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in the narrator's tone over the course of the text?
options: From amused tolerance of the keepers to open anger directed at Pavel's impatience.
From routine detachment toward the rule to restrained but pointed disapproval of it.
From nervous uncertainty about her skills to confident pride in her translation work.
From warm admiration for the station chief to quiet regret about leaving the station.
items.explanation: 처음에 화자는 규칙을 '수백 개의 규정처럼' 담담하게 통역하며 감정 없는 태도를 보인다. 그러나 나흘째 Pavel이 계단참에서 몇 시간씩 기다리는 모습을 본 뒤, 목소리가 '평평하고 신중해지며' 규칙을 누그러뜨리지 않고 그 부조리함을 그대로 전한다. 따라서 무심함에서 절제된 비판으로 바뀐다는 B가 정답이다. A는 분노의 대상을 Pavel로 잘못 잡았고, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없는 감정 변화를 제시한다.

items.passage:
When you left the noodle stall on Hamra Street last Thursday, Karim, you were certain I had lied to the old cook. I understand why. He asked, in Arabic, whether I was your mother, and you heard me answer with something much longer than 'no.' You assumed I had claimed a title I have not earned. I was annoyed, I admit, that you would not let me explain on the walk home; I even rehearsed a little speech about trust and fairness. But I have since thought about your face at the counter, how quickly the steam hid it, and I am less interested in being right. What I actually said was 'I am the one who gets to feed him today.' My Arabic is clumsy, and perhaps it sounded like more. If it did, I am sorry. Come back to the stall with me on Sunday, and you can ask him yourself what he heard.

Imani
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone of the letter shifts?
options: From cheerful nostalgia about the stall to bitter disappointment in Karim's behavior.
From formal politeness toward Karim to playful teasing about his poor Arabic.
From defensive irritation over Karim's suspicion to gentle, conciliatory openness.
From confident authority as a parent to anxious doubt about her own memory.
items.explanation: Imani는 처음에 Karim이 설명을 듣지 않은 것에 '짜증이 났다'고 인정하고 신뢰에 관한 연설까지 준비했다고 말한다. 그러나 'But' 이후 Karim의 표정을 떠올리며 옳고 그름보다 화해에 관심을 두고, 사과와 함께 다시 가게에 가자고 제안한다. 따라서 방어적 짜증에서 부드러운 화해로 바뀐다는 C가 정답이다. B는 아랍어가 서툰 사람을 Karim으로 잘못 보았고, A와 D는 지문의 감정 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Mumbai has never felt so loud to me as it did this evening on the field behind the school. March 14. I stayed after practice again because Ishaan stays, kicking a ball against the broken goalpost until the light goes orange. Six weeks now without a single word to me, to anyone. I have tried questions, jokes, silence of my own. Tonight I was tired and, honestly, a little resentful; I wrote attendance notes on my knee and told myself a teacher cannot rescue every child. Then the ball rolled to my feet. I pushed it back badly, and he said, 'Your left foot is terrible, Miss Tara.' Five words. I laughed so hard the groundskeeper looked over from the far gate. I am writing this by lamplight and still grinning, though I keep warning myself not to expect another sentence tomorrow.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the diary entry?
options: From hopeful excitement about Ishaan's progress to worried frustration at his silence.
From playful humor about soccer practice to serious concern about the groundskeeper.
From calm professional distance to sharp anger at Ishaan's teasing remark.
From weary, somewhat bitter resignation to delighted but cautious joy.
items.explanation: Tara는 처음에 지치고 '조금 원망스러웠다'며 교사가 모든 아이를 구할 수는 없다고 체념한다. Ishaan이 다섯 단어를 말한 뒤 그녀는 크게 웃고 여전히 미소 짓지만, 내일 또 말을 기대하지 말자고 스스로를 다잡는다. 따라서 지친 체념에서 기쁘지만 조심스러운 기쁨으로 바뀐다는 D가 정답이다. A는 변화의 방향이 반대이고, C는 놀림에 대한 반응을 분노로 잘못 읽었다.

items.passage: By the seventh evening of the rainy season, Kwesi had climbed the stairs to Obinna's projection booth for the seventh time, carrying the same cracked lens wrapped in cloth. Obinna, who mended everything in the old Accra cinema from ceiling fans to torn film, laughed at him each time. 'A lens is like an egg,' he said. 'Once broken, you may glue it, but you will not hatch anything.' Still Kwesi came, and still Obinna glued, and the townspeople began to joke that the two men were rehearsing a comedy. On the seventh evening, however, Obinna held the lens to the projector's beam and saw, through the crack, the screen below split into two pictures, one bright and one dim. He did not laugh. He asked Kwesi whose face had been in the last film shown through it. Kwesi answered that it was his late mother's, and Obinna set down his glue and said nothing for a long time.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From lighthearted mockery of Kwesi's visits to solemn, respectful understanding.
From suspicious hostility toward Kwesi to warm, comic friendship between the men.
From tense urgency about the damaged lens to relieved celebration of its repair.
From reverent awe at the cinema's history to playful teasing about its machines.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Obinna는 매번 웃으며 깨진 렌즈를 달걀에 비유하고, 마을 사람들은 두 사람이 희극을 연습한다고 농담한다. 그러나 'however' 이후 Obinna는 웃지 않고 렌즈에 비친 마지막 얼굴을 묻고, 그것이 Kwesi의 돌아가신 어머니였다는 답에 오래 침묵한다. 따라서 가벼운 조롱에서 엄숙한 이해로 바뀐다는 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 변화의 방향을 거꾸로 제시하고, C는 수리의 성공을 축하하는 장면이 없으므로 틀리다.

items.passage: We had not sat side by side since we were children, Thuy and I, and now the narrow compartment of the little coastal train on Jeju Island forced our knees together. I watched the black volcanic walls slide past and tried to remember the summer she had taught me to swim off Hamdeok. At the funeral that morning, she had stood with her husband's family instead of ours, bowing at their pace, wearing their white ribbon. My aunts had noticed; they noticed everything. Halfway to Seongsan, Thuy took out a paper bag of tangerines, the kind our grandmother used to peel for us in one long spiral. She handed me one without a word. I peeled it the old way, badly, and she corrected my thumb exactly as Grandmother had. Neither of us mentioned the ribbon.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: The narrator describes an open quarrel at the funeral, then explains how the aunts later resolved it.
The narrator recalls a shared past, notes a present rift, then depicts a quiet reconnection.
The narrator praises Thuy's new in-laws, then questions the customs the family observed at the funeral.
The narrator lists the sights along the train route, then reveals why the trip had to be cut short.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 어린 시절 Thuy가 수영을 가르쳐 준 여름을 회상한다. 이어 장례식에서 Thuy가 남편 가족 편에 서 이모들이 이를 주목했다는 현재의 거리감을 보여 준다. 마지막으로 할머니처럼 귤 껍질 벗기는 법을 바로잡아 주는 장면으로 말없는 재결합을 그린다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, A는 공개적 다툼과 이모들의 해결이 없고, C와 D는 지문에 없는 내용이다.

items.passage: By noon the barge had run aground on the white crust where the old salt works outside Lyon had flooded and dried a dozen times. Wanjiru, its captain, found the stowaway behind the brine barrels: a girl of perhaps sixteen named Solange, who said she had run from a boarding school and had a little brother waiting at the far landing. Wanjiru meant to march her straight to the gendarmes. Instead, crouched on the salt while the crew dug at the hull, she listened to Solange argue with herself about what to tell the boy. The truth would frighten him; a lie would have to be kept up for years. Wanjiru, who had once told her own sister that their father was merely 'at sea,' found that she had opinions. By the time the barge floated free at dusk, the two of them had written three versions of the story on the back of a cargo manifest, and crossed out every one.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a dispute between two members of the crew, then shows the captain punishing both of them.
It describes the salt works in detail, then traces the history of the barge's many groundings.
It sets up a clash over authority, then shifts toward a shared dilemma the characters work through.
It recounts Solange's escape from the boarding school, then reveals that her brother was never waiting.
items.explanation: 처음에 선장 Wanjiru는 밀항자 Solange를 헌병에게 넘기려 하므로 권위와 위반의 충돌이 제시된다. 이후 Solange가 동생에게 무엇을 말할지 고민하는 것을 듣고, 자신도 비슷한 거짓말을 한 경험 때문에 함께 이야기를 여러 번 써 보는 장면으로 초점이 옮겨 간다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 Solange가 선원이 아니며 처벌도 없고, D는 동생이 없었다는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: I thought my mother-in-law disliked me for the first year of my marriage. Adaeze ran the small printing press her late husband had opened in the Médina of Dakar, and on my wedding day she gave me a ream of blank cream paper, tied with twine, and nothing else. Kwame laughed when I asked what it meant; he said his mother was practical. I took it as a judgment: here is emptiness, fill it if you can. For months I left the ream untouched in a closet. Then, one hot afternoon, I visited the press room to bring Kwame lunch and saw Adaeze guiding a sheet of that same cream paper through the rollers, printing a wedding program for a stranger. She told me that every bride in her family received paper from the shop's first order, so that she could write the family's next chapter. I went home and opened the ream. Now I see how quickly I read insult into silence, and how rarely I ask before deciding.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: The author explains the long history of a family printing press, then describes how it nearly closed.
The author criticizes an old family custom, then argues that new brides ought to reject such gifts.
The author describes her husband's teasing, then recounts how she finally persuaded him to apologize.
The author recounts a misreading, then a discovery, then reflects on a habit of her own.
items.explanation: 필자는 먼저 시어머니의 빈 종이 선물을 자신에 대한 평가로 오해했다고 말한다. 이어 인쇄소에서 그 종이가 가족의 다음 장을 쓰라는 전통임을 알게 되는 발견이 나온다. 끝으로 침묵을 모욕으로 성급히 읽는 자신의 습관을 돌아본다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, A·B·C는 인쇄소의 폐업, 관습 비판, 남편의 사과처럼 지문에 없는 전개를 제시한다.

items.passage: Years later, I still cannot walk past a school music room without hearing Marcel's old upright piano, the one with the sticking D. He had taught me there when I was eleven, and when I returned to Rotterdam at thirty, the school was planning to sell the piano and turn the room into storage. Marcel, retired and stooped, asked me to help. Our plan was simple: I would play a concert for the parents' council and remind them what the room was for. It worked. The council voted to keep the room and the piano, and the headmaster shook our hands. Afterward Marcel and I sat in the empty room among folded chairs. He pressed the sticking D, and it stuck. He said the room would be kept, but no one had been hired to teach in it. I understood then that we had saved a shell, and that neither of us had wanted only that.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It introduces a remembered place, recounts a successful effort to save it, then exposes a hollow result.
It describes a childhood music lesson in detail, then explains why the narrator gave up the piano entirely.
It presents the headmaster's plan for the room, then shows how Marcel and the narrator defeated it in court.
It recounts a concert for the parents' council, then shifts to the narrator's doubts about her own talent.
items.explanation: 지문은 화자가 기억하는 음악실과 피아노를 소개하며 시작한다. 이어 연주회 계획이 성공해 위원회가 음악실을 유지하기로 결정하는 과정이 나온다. 그러나 그 뒤 가르칠 사람이 없다는 말과 여전히 걸리는 D 건반을 통해 결과가 공허하다는 점이 드러난다. 따라서 A가 정답이며, C의 법정 다툼이나 D의 재능에 대한 의심은 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Sizzle and hiss filled the camp dining hall each dawn, along with the smell of sweet bread and frying eggs, for Tui was the youngest cook ever trusted with the great iron griddle on Maui. Her aunt Astrid, who ran the kitchen and rarely smiled, had decided that Tui's grandmother should leave her house on the windy ridge and move into the room behind the pantry. Tui said the old woman would fade away far from the sea. Astrid said the ridge would kill her first. For a week they argued only through food: Tui burned Astrid's toast; Astrid oversalted Tui's rice. Then a storm cut the ridge road, and both of them drove up together with a pot of soup. They found the grandmother calmly mending a net, and she told them that a tree should be moved only by those who will water it afterward. Driving down, aunt and niece agreed to take turns.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes the kitchen's daily routine, then explains how the camp chose its youngest ever cook.
It sets up a disagreement, shows it escalating, then resolves it through an elder's guidance.
It presents the grandmother's wisdom, then shows Tui and Astrid rejecting her advice outright.
It introduces a storm on the ridge, then flashes back to explain why the ridge road was built.
items.explanation: 지문은 할머니를 옮길지에 대한 Tui와 Astrid의 의견 차이를 먼저 제시한다. 이어 일주일 동안 음식으로 다투는 장면으로 갈등이 고조된다. 폭풍 뒤 함께 찾아간 할머니의 나무 비유를 듣고 두 사람이 번갈아 돌보기로 합의하며 갈등이 풀린다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, C는 조언을 거부했다고 했으므로 결말과 반대이고, A와 D는 지문의 초점이 아니다.

items.passage: Was it foolish to bring a cabbage to a hospital? Sunethra, who farmed the steep plot above the fjord, had wrapped it in newspaper anyway and now held it on her knees in the waiting room in Bergen. Across from her sat Amelia, the city surveyor who had measured Sunethra's land last spring and declared half of it too steep to farm. Amelia's father was in surgery; so was Sunethra's neighbor. 'That's from the lower terrace?' Amelia asked. 'The upper,' Sunethra said, shrugging. 'The part your map calls unusable. It's nothing special.' __She turned the cabbage slightly so that its tightest, palest leaves faced the surveyor.__ Amelia studied it for a while, then took out a pencil and, on the back of an appointment card, began to redraw a line.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that Sunethra is embarrassed by the cabbage and hopes Amelia will ignore it.
It suggests that Sunethra intends to give the cabbage to Amelia's father after surgery.
It reveals that Sunethra's dismissive words conceal her pride in what her land produced.
It indicates that Sunethra has decided to sell the upper terrace to the city surveyor.
items.explanation: Sunethra는 어깨를 으쓱하며 '특별할 것 없다'고 말하지만, 그 양배추는 Amelia의 지도가 쓸모없다고 한 위쪽 계단밭에서 자란 것이다. 밑줄 문장에서 그녀는 가장 좋은 잎이 측량사를 향하도록 양배추를 돌려, 말과 달리 자부심을 드러낸다. 이후 Amelia가 선을 다시 그리기 시작하는 것도 이 행동의 효과를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 C가 정답이며, A는 자부심을 부끄러움으로 잘못 읽었다.

items.passage: Steam from the espresso machine fogged the window of the station café, and the radio behind the counter played a calypso Kiara had not heard in twenty years. Felix's suitcase leaned against her chair. He was talking about dorm rooms and bus passes, and she was nodding, but her hand kept returning to her bag, where a brass compass rested in a velvet pouch. It had belonged to Felix's grandfather, who had lent it to her the summer she left Port of Spain for a job in Toronto, telling her to bring it back when she knew her way. She never had. __She had carried it through four apartments and two countries, and she had never once needed it.__ When the train was called, she pressed the pouch into Felix's palm and closed his fingers over it. 'Borrowed,' she said. 'Not given.'
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Kiara regrets moving abroad instead of staying with her father.
It suggests that the compass is broken and therefore of no practical use to Felix.
It emphasizes that Kiara has finally learned how to navigate unfamiliar cities.
It implies that Kiara valued the compass as a bond rather than as a practical tool.
items.explanation: 나침반은 Kiara의 아버지가 길을 알게 되면 돌려 달라며 빌려준 물건이다. 밑줄 문장은 그녀가 한 번도 필요하지 않았는데도 여러 집과 나라를 거치며 지녔다고 말해, 나침반이 길잡이 도구가 아니라 아버지와의 연결이었음을 암시한다. 마지막에 '빌려준 것'이라며 아들에게 건네는 장면이 이를 이어 간다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, B의 고장이나 A의 후회는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: We found the letters in a biscuit tin beneath the workbench of our mother's radio repair shop in Marrakesh, a week after the funeral. My brother Yiannis read them aloud while I, Yasmin, sorted vacuum tubes into egg cartons. Most were from a man identified only by an initial, thanking her for fixing his radio without charge, again and again, for eleven years. Yiannis grew quiet; I knew what he was thinking. A free repair every month starts to look like a secret. __Then I remembered how she used to leave a radio playing by the shop door at night, turned low, tuned to the station that read the news for the blind.__ I went back through the tin and found, at the bottom, a receipt from a school for the blind, signed with the same initial. Our mother, I think now, was not hiding anything; she was simply listening for someone.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a memory that leads the narrator to rethink a suspicious reading.
It shows that the narrator agrees with Yiannis that their mother kept a romantic secret.
It describes the shop's nightly routine to emphasize how successful the business became.
It reveals the narrator's resentment that their mother spent her evenings away from home.
items.explanation: 앞에서 남매는 11년간 이어진 무료 수리를 어떤 비밀로 의심하기 시작한다. 밑줄 문장은 시각장애인용 뉴스 방송을 틀어 두던 어머니의 기억을 떠올리게 하고, 화자는 이를 계기로 상자를 다시 뒤져 맹학교 영수증을 찾는다. 즉 이 기억이 의심스러운 해석을 다시 생각하게 만드는 전환점이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 화자가 오빠의 의심에 동의한다고 했으므로 반대이고, C와 D는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: 'Nobody pays for dovetails anymore,' Alba said during my first week in the rented farmhouse in Galicia where she kept her carpentry shop. I was nineteen, and Ivan was the name she shouted whenever a clamp slipped, which was often. Her grandfather had founded the business; the lease, she admitted, ran out in spring, and the bank preferred customers who bought flat-pack furniture. Still, every morning she made me cut joints by hand until my palms blistered. __One evening I found her ledger open on the bench, with every column of the last year totaled in red.__ I said nothing about it. The next morning she handed me the chisel again, and I began to see that she was not training a worker for her shop. She was training someone to carry its craft somewhere else after the doors closed.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It suggests that Alba is hiding the shop's wealth from the narrator to avoid paying him more.
It provides evidence that undercuts Alba's hopes and reframes her insistence on training.
It shows that the narrator secretly plans to take over the shop's accounts from Alba.
It marks the moment when the narrator decides to quit his apprenticeship for good.
items.explanation: 앞에서 임대가 봄에 끝나고 은행이 조립식 가구를 선호한다는 위기가 제시된다. 밑줄 문장의 빨간 장부는 가게가 살아남기 어렵다는 증거를 보여 준다. 그 뒤 화자는 Alba의 고된 훈련이 가게를 위한 것이 아니라 가게가 문을 닫은 뒤에도 기술을 이어 갈 사람을 키우는 것임을 깨닫는다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, A는 장부가 적자를 보여 주므로 반대이고, D는 화자가 다음 날도 끌을 받으므로 틀리다.

items.passage: Grapes do not hurry. So said Vesna, the strictest violin teacher in the hills above Tbilisi, who held her lessons among the vines at harvest so that her pupils would learn patience from the fruit. Anushka, her newest student, wanted to play fast. Each afternoon she raced through her scales, and each afternoon Vesna made her begin again, slower, while the pickers' baskets filled around them. On the last day of harvest, Anushka played a folk tune the pickers sang, quickly and brightly, and the pickers clapped and danced between the rows. Vesna said nothing. __That evening, she set aside the slow études she had planned for the winter and wrote out three dances in her own hand.__ In the morning she gave them to Anushka and told her that some fruit is for wine and some is for eating straight from the vine.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that Vesna has grown impatient with Anushka and plans to stop teaching her.
It reveals that Vesna intends to perform the dances herself at the pickers' celebration.
It indicates that Vesna has silently revised her view of how Anushka should be taught.
It explains that the slow études were too difficult for a student of Anushka's age.
items.explanation: Vesna는 처음에 '포도는 서두르지 않는다'며 Anushka에게 느리게 연습하도록 반복해서 요구한다. Anushka의 빠른 민요 연주에 일꾼들이 춤추는 것을 본 뒤 Vesna는 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 밑줄 문장에서 그녀가 느린 연습곡을 치우고 춤곡을 직접 적는 것은 말없이 교육 방침을 바꾸었음을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이며, A와 D는 근거가 없고 B는 춤곡을 Anushka에게 준다는 내용과 어긋난다.

## 문항
### lit40-medium-01-048 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Four hours a day, six days a week, no recordings: those were Ananya's conditions when she agreed to teach me. We met in the guesthouse of a small monastery on the edge of Mumbai, where the monks let her use a whitewashed room in exchange for playing at their evening prayers. She taught a way of tuning and bowing that her own teacher had learned in a village whose name I could not find on any map. Nobody else I knew played like that anymore. When I asked why she would not let me record her, she said a tape would teach my ears but not my hands. Vikram, she would say, again, and correct my wrist with a pencil tap until I hated the sound of it. Only much later did I see that the old style lived in her fingers like a language with one speaker left.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “a language with one speaker left” most nearly suggests that the old style was
A) a technique so complex that it needed translation
B) a kind of music Ananya refused to share with others
C) a rare practice kept alive almost entirely by one person
D) a habit Ananya found difficult to explain in words

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
지문은 그 연주법이 지도에도 없는 마을에서 전해졌고 이제 그렇게 연주하는 사람이 거의 없다고 말한다. 따라서 화자 한 명만 남은 언어라는 비유는 거의 한 사람에 의해서만 이어지는 사라져 가는 기술을 뜻하며 C가 정답이다. A는 '언어'를 번역과 연결한 오답이고, B는 녹음을 거부한 점만 보고 Ananya가 직접 가르친다는 사실을 놓친 것이다. D는 그녀가 말 대신 손으로 가르친 장면을 지나치게 해석한 것이다.
### lit40-medium-01-049 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
So you let me win, Edith said, the moment Faisal stepped onto the old stone bridge. They had not spoken in nine years, not since the summer their grandmother set them to race across the Cornish headland for her silver whistle. Faisal had been faster; everyone knew it. Yet a stride from the bridge he had stumbled, and Edith had touched the parapet first. Now the grandmother lay in the churchyard behind them, and the whistle hung at Edith's neck. All these years, she said, the prize had felt like borrowed bread, filling her mouth but never her stomach. Faisal looked down at the river. He told her he had seen how badly she needed something of her own that year. Edith unhooked the whistle and pressed it into his palm, and for once he did not give it back.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “borrowed bread” most nearly suggests that Edith's victory was
A) a gift she had been eager to return to her grandmother long ago
B) a reward she had always been required to share with Faisal
C) a prize whose value faded slowly as she grew older
D) a win she could not fully enjoy because it was not earned

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
Edith는 더 빠른 Faisal이 결승 직전에 일부러 넘어져 이겼다는 사실을 알고 있었다. 빌린 빵이 입은 채워도 배는 채우지 못했다는 표현은 스스로 얻지 않은 승리라 진정한 만족을 주지 못했다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 할머니에게 돌려주려 했다는 근거가 없고, B는 '빌렸다'를 공유로 오해한 것이다. C는 시간이 흐르며 가치가 줄었다는 해석으로, 처음부터 공허했다는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-01-057 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Smell of wet soil and crushed shiso rose around them as Shigeru and Chiyo knelt in their plot of the community garden in Kyoto, pulling weeds between the rows of eggplant. For an hour they joked about their last concert, where the audience had numbered eleven, including a sleeping baby, and Chiyo imitated the hall manager's sigh until Shigeru dropped his trowel laughing. Then she mentioned the letter. A conservatory in Vienna had offered her a full scholarship beginning in January; it covered one student, not a duo. Shigeru went on weeding. He asked, evenly, when she would need to answer, and whether her cello would travel in the hold or on a seat. Each question was polite and practical, and each one seemed to set him a little further from her.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
A) From bitter complaint about the concert to warm encouragement
B) From playful teasing to guarded restraint after Chiyo's news
C) From nervous tension to calm acceptance of a shared plan
D) From nostalgic reflection to open celebration of Chiyo's success

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
앞부분에서 두 사람은 관객 열한 명이었던 공연을 두고 농담하며 웃는다. Chiyo가 혼자만 받을 수 있는 장학금 소식을 꺼내자 Shigeru는 담담하고 실무적인 질문만 하며 감정을 감춘다. 따라서 장난스러운 분위기에서 절제되고 경계하는 분위기로 바뀌는 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 격려나 축하를, C는 함께 세운 계획을 말하지만 지문의 거리감과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-01-058 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Once, I loved the library on Central Avenue
for its hush, its radiators ticking like patient clocks,
the way Elan would leave me in the stacks
and read the paper by the window, never hurrying.
We had a rhythm there: I chose, he signed.
Then on a Saturday in March he said,
between the atlases and the encyclopedias,
that he had sold the house, that we would move
to Denver in June, that it was settled.
Settled. As if I were a column he had added.
Now the radiators only hiss.
The books lean on each other like strangers in a line.
I, Nayeli, twelve, take down a map
and trace a road I did not choose.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the poem?
A) From restless boredom to eager curiosity about a new city
B) From quiet fear to comforting reassurance from Elan
C) From fond nostalgia to resentful bitterness after Elan's news
D) From playful humor to calm resignation about the move

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
앞부분에서 화자는 도서관의 고요함과 Elan과의 리듬을 애정 어린 회상으로 그린다. Elan이 묻지도 않고 이사를 결정했다고 말한 뒤, 화자는 'Settled'를 되뇌며 자신을 더해진 숫자 한 줄에 비유하고, 라디에이터는 '쉭쉭거리기만' 한다. 따라서 애정 어린 그리움에서 원망 섞인 씁쓸함으로 바뀌는 C가 정답이다. D는 체념으로 보일 수 있지만 원망이 드러나는 표현을 놓쳤고, A와 B는 지문에 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-01-059 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
BARTOLO: They printed your name alone, Judge, on the front page.
(Evening. The iron gate of a cemetery in Surabaya. LAN, a retired judge, leans on her cane. BARTOLO, her young clerk, holds a folded newspaper.)
LAN: (lightly) Newspapers like a single name. It fits the column better.
BARTOLO: I drafted three hundred pages of that opinion. You know I did.
LAN: (still amused) And I signed them. That is how it is done, my boy.
BARTOLO: My father is buried here. I promised him our family name would mean something one day. (He holds out the paper.) Read it to him.
(LAN stops smiling. A long pause. She takes the newspaper, studies it, then lowers it.)
LAN: (quietly) Give me your pen. Tomorrow I will write to the editor myself, and the correction will carry both our names.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
A) From fierce anger to forced cheerfulness at the gate
B) From shared grief to hopeful celebration of the ruling
C) From formal respect to open hostility between the two
D) From dismissive amusement to sober acknowledgment of the clerk

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
처음에 Lan은 '가볍게', '여전히 재미있다는 듯' 말하며 Bartolo의 기여를 관행이라고 넘긴다. Bartolo가 아버지의 무덤 앞에서 신문을 읽어 달라고 하자, 지문은 Lan이 웃음을 멈추고 오래 침묵한 뒤 '조용히' 말한다고 지시한다. 따라서 무시하는 듯한 여유에서 진지한 인정으로 바뀌는 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 분노, 축하, 적대감처럼 지문에 없는 감정을 내세운다.
### lit40-medium-01-060 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Three chairs, two mirrors, one radio tuned to the shipping forecast: that is the whole of Winston's barbershop on a narrow lane in Taipei, and for years I came less for the haircut than for his stories. He had been a sailor for thirty years, and he told those years like jokes: the typhoon off Okinawa, the cook who kept a parrot, the captain who could not swim. Last month, when I came in, Bokhee from the noodle stall next door was already in the chair, and Winston was laughing at something she had said. Then she asked about his nephew's boat, the one that had gone out in August and come back with half its crew. Winston set the scissors down. He finished her haircut without another word, and when I took her place, he cut my hair the way one folds a letter one does not want to reread.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
A) From lively storytelling to heavy silence when a recent loss is raised
B) From bitter regret to amused acceptance of his years at sea
C) From casual friendliness to open anger at Bokhee's rudeness
D) From nervous chatter to calm confidence about his nephew's future

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]

B) It reveals that Vesna intends to perform the dances herself at the pickers' celebration.
